GAP [1]: A comprehensive understanding of the interplay between KRAS mutations and the tumor microenvironment in driving resistance to KRAS inhibitors is missing, and it matters because elucidating this relationship could reveal novel therapeutic targets to enhance treatment efficacy.
GAP [2]: There is a lack of clinical trials investigating the efficacy of combination therapies involving KRAS inhibitors and other targeted agents, such as farnesyl-transferase inhibitors or immune-based therapies, and it matters because these combinations may overcome resistance mechanisms and improve patient outcomes.
GAP [3]: The role of epigenetic mechanisms in driving resistance to KRAS inhibitors is not well understood, and it matters because identifying epigenetic alterations could lead to the development of epigenetic therapies that enhance the durability of response to KRAS inhibitors.
GAP [4]: A systematic analysis of the molecular characteristics of KRAS-mutant tumors that are most likely to develop resistance to KRAS inhibitors is missing, and it matters because such an analysis could enable the identification of biomarkers for predicting treatment response and resistance.
GAP [5]: The impact of KRAS inhibitor resistance on the metabolic and bioenergetic profiles of cancer cells is not well characterized, and it matters because understanding these changes could reveal novel vulnerabilities that can be targeted to overcome resistance and improve treatment outcomes.
